info.title: Myota API
info.summary: Programmes, places, activations, awards — one API, two audiences.
info.description:
The composed contract for every Myota service. It is generated from
`contracts/core.openapi.yaml`, `contracts/geodata.openapi.yaml` and
`contracts/activity.openapi.yaml`, so it cannot describe a route that no
service implements without the build failing.

**Two audiences.** `/v1/auth/**`, `/v1/me/**`, `/v1/activations/**`,
`/v1/qsos/**`, `/v1/awards/**`, `/v1/proposals/**` and `/v1/statistics/me`
are participant routes. `/v1/admin/**` is administrator routes, and requires
a session issued by `POST /v1/admin/auth/login`, which is MFA-gated. The
audience is a claim in the token, checked at the gateway before the request is
proxied — it is not a client-side convention and not a separate host.

**Errors** are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457), always with a `type`, a
`title`, a `status` and a `requestId` that matches `X-Request-ID`.

**Collections** return `{ items, nextCursor }` and are cursor-paginated.
`nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.

**Mutations** accept `Idempotency-Key`. A replay with the same key and body
returns the stored response and creates nothing.

**Edits to spatial entities** carry the `revision` they were read at.
A stale revision is `409 about:blank#revision-conflict`, never a silent
overwrite.

Event schemas — the payloads services exchange — are published alongside this
document under `contracts/events/`; they are not HTTP operations and so do not
appear here.

servers.description: Test environment, participant host. The same gateway serves both hosts; the host decides which application the browser loaded, not which API.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Participant registration, sign-in and credential recovery. Public by necessity — everything here is reachable without a session.

tags.name: admin-auth
tags.description: Administrator sign-in. Separate endpoints, separate session, MFA required. A participant login can never produce an administrator session.

tags.name: me
tags.description: The signed-in account — its profile, callsigns and inbox.

tags.name: programmes
tags.description: Programmes, their public content pages, and their policy.

tags.name: admin-identity
tags.description: Two administration surfaces, not one. Admins grant authority and are the escalation path; participants are day-to-day support at volume. Different scopes, different guard rails, never one "Users" screen.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: The single notification ledger. One table for email and in-app, one retry policy, one dead-letter path.

tags.name: entities
tags.description: The catalogue. Public reads are anonymous; writes need `geodata.edit`.

tags.name: proposals
tags.description: Participant-submitted corrections and new places. A proposal is a request for review, not an edit — participants cannot write the catalogue.

tags.name: imports
tags.description: Resumable uploads, import runs, candidates, conflation and promotion. Administrator only.

tags.name: sources
tags.description: Data providers, their snapshots and their schedules. Administrator only.

tags.name: tiles
tags.description: Vector tiles for the public map. Anonymous.

tags.name: activations
tags.description: An activation at a place: start, read, close, cancel. Participant routes, scoped to the caller's own activations.

tags.name: qsos
tags.description: Contacts logged against an activation, and the correction requests that change them.

tags.name: log-imports
tags.description: ADIF and CSV uploads that create QSOs in bulk, with a per-row outcome so a rejected line is visible rather than silently dropped.

tags.name: awards
tags.description: Award definitions, progress, requests and issuance. Definitions are administrator-owned; requests are the participant's.

tags.name: statistics
tags.description: Materialised snapshots and leaderboards, per account, programme or entity.

post.description:
Creates a `pending` account and sends a verification email. The account
cannot sign in until the address is verified, and an unverified account
is swept after seven days — a mistyped address must not permanently block
the person who owns it.

Duplicate addresses are rejected by a `citext` unique index and produce
the same generic response as a successful registration, so registration
cannot be used to enumerate accounts.

202.description: Accepted. The same response is returned whether or not the address was already registered.

403.description: Registration is closed. The `type` is `about:blank#registration-disabled`; this is one setting, not a flow gated on an environment variable.

post.summary: Verify an address with the token from the email
post.description:
Marks the address verified and activates the account. The token is
single-use and is re-checked against the account's current address, so it
cannot be used after the address changed.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The token is single-use; a replay returns the same success and creates nothing.

200.description: The address is verified and the account is active.

410.description: The token expired or was already used.

post.description: Invalidates any earlier verification token for the account, so only the newest link works. Always answers `202`, whether or not the address is registered.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Rate-limited per account; repeating it is the same request, not a second effect.

post.description:
Issues a participant session. The token carries `aud=participant`, which
the gateway refuses on `/v1/admin/**`. Wrong password and unknown address
take the same time and return the same message — the two failures must be
indistinguishable.

A locked account answers `429` until the lock expires; the lockout counter
lives in the database because it has to be authoritative across replicas.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Authenticating twice legitimately creates two sessions.

200.description: Signed in. The refresh token is set as `__Host-myota_sid`.

post.description:
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token. A rotated token
stays usable for a 30 second grace window and returns the same new token,
so a lost response on a flaky connection does not cost the user their
session. Reuse after that window revokes the whole session and records a
`refresh_reuse` security event.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Rotation carries its own replay protection; a caller-supplied key would add a second mechanism.

200.description: A new access token, and a new refresh cookie.

post.summary: Sign out of the participant session
post.description: Revokes the session and adds the access token's `jti` to the revocation list.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Revoking an already revoked session is a no-op.

post.description: Sends a reset link if the address is registered. Always `202`, so the endpoint cannot be used to find out who has an account.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Always accepted; issuing a second token supersedes the first.

post.description: Consumes the reset token, sets the new password and revokes every session belonging to the account. There is no "keep me signed in" path: a reset means the old credential is suspect.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The reset token is single-use.

204.description: The password is changed and all sessions are revoked.

410.description: The token expired or was already used.

post.description:
Sends a confirmation link to the **new** address. The account keeps the
old address until that link is used, so a typo cannot lock the owner out.
The request needs the current password — a stolen session alone must not
be able to move an account to an attacker's mailbox.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Rate-limited per account; a second request supersedes the first token.

202.description: A confirmation email has been sent to the new address.

post.description: Moves the account to the new address and marks it verified. The token is bound to both the account and the new address, so a token issued for one address cannot be used for another.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The token is single-use.

200.description: The address is changed and verified.

410.description: The token expired or was already used.

get.description: Every session for the account, newest first, so a suspicious one can be identified by user agent and address and revoked on its own rather than by signing out everywhere.

delete.summary: Revoke one of the participant's sessions
delete.description: Revokes a single session. Revoking the current one is the same as signing out.

post.description:
Checks the password, then answers one of two things: a challenge, or a
session. A session is only issued when the account already has a
confirmed second factor — there is no flag, environment variable, or
development mode that skips this. A brand-new administrator is
provisioned by another administrator and enrols through
`/v1/admin/auth/mfa/enrol` on first sign-in.

The response is discriminated on `status` rather than modelling the
challenge as an error, because needing a second factor is the expected
path, not a failure.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Authenticating twice legitimately creates two sessions.

200.description: `status: mfa_required` with a challenge, or `status: authenticated` with a session when the account has confirmed a factor and the challenge is satisfied.

authenticated.summary: A passkey satisfied the challenge during sign-in

403.description:
The password is correct and the account cannot sign in for one of two
reasons. The distinction is in `type` because the repairs differ: one
needs another administrator, the other needs the account owner.

- `about:blank#mfa-not-enrolled` — no confirmed second factor. The
  account cannot sign in until one is enrolled, and enrolment requires
  an existing session, so a newly provisioned administrator is given
  their factor by whoever provisioned them.
- `about:blank#forbidden` — no role with an administrator scope. A
  participant account cannot be promoted by guessing at this endpoint.

A `403` therefore says the password was right. That is a deliberate
disclosure: the alternative is an administrator who cannot tell "wrong
password" from "your factor is missing", and the address is already
known to the caller who holds its password.

value.title: Second factor not enrolled
value.detail: No second factor is enrolled for this account. Enrol one before signing in.

value.title: Not an administrator account
value.detail: This account holds no role with an administrator scope.

post.description: Completes a sign-in started by `POST /v1/admin/auth/login`. A recovery code is consumed on use; a TOTP code is rejected if it was already used in the current step window.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The challenge id is single-use and bound to one password verification.

401.description: The code was wrong, or was already used in its step window. The challenge stays open until its attempt limit is reached, so a typo costs one of five attempts rather than the sign-in. Type `about:blank#mfa-failed`.

410.description: The challenge expired. Start the sign-in again.

post.description: Same rotation and grace window as the participant refresh, with the shorter administrator lifetimes — 10 minute access, 30 minute idle.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Rotation carries its own replay protection.

200.description: A new access token, and a new refresh cookie.

post.summary: Sign out of the administrator session
post.x-idempotency-reason: Revoking an already revoked session is a no-op.

post.description:
Role changes, MFA resets and account suspensions require a
re-authentication within the last five minutes. This endpoint records
one. The grant is bound to the session, not to the token, so a stolen
access token cannot manufacture freshness.

Without this, a stolen administrator session is enough to grant the
attacker an administrator role of their own — escalation that leaves no
trace until it is used.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Recording freshness twice is the same state.

200.description: The session is fresh until the stated time.

post.description:
Returns a TOTP secret and its `otpauth://` URI, plus ten one-time
recovery codes. Nothing is confirmed until
`/v1/admin/auth/mfa/enrol/confirm` succeeds, so an interrupted enrolment
cannot leave an administrator locked out with a secret they never stored.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Re-enrolment replaces the pending secret; only a confirmed factor is durable.

post.summary: Confirm second-factor enrolment with a code
post.description: Marks the factor confirmed. From this moment the account can sign in; before it, `/v1/admin/auth/login` refuses to issue a session.
post.x-idempotency-reason: A confirmed factor cannot be confirmed twice; the second attempt is refused.

get.description: Works for either audience. The `audience` field says which login produced the session, which is what the two front ends use to decide whether to offer the admin console at all.

patch.description: Only the display name. Email changes go through `/v1/auth/email/change`, which proves control of the new address; a profile update must not be able to move an account to an address the caller has not verified.

post.summary: Add a callsign to the account
post.description: A new callsign starts `UNVERIFIED`. It can be used to sign activations only after an administrator has reviewed the evidence, so claiming a famous callsign does not grant its history.

delete.summary: Remove a callsign from the account
delete.description: Retires the callsign rather than deleting the row, so an activation that used it keeps its history.

put.description: The primary callsign is what other users see and what a new activation defaults to. `PUT` because the operation sets one value: repeating it leaves the same state.

get.description: The `in_app` channel of the single notification ledger. Email deliveries appear in the administrator view, not here.

200.description: One page of notifications, newest first.

post.summary: Mark an inbox notification as read
post.x-idempotency-reason: Setting a read timestamp twice yields the same timestamp.

get.description: Anonymous. Only `active` programmes are listed here; drafts and archived programmes are visible to administrators through the same endpoint with the `status` filter.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Administrator only for anything other than `active`.

get.description: Anonymous. Slug, not id, because the slug is what appears in links and what a user can remember.

get.summary: List a programme's published content pages

200.description: The page, with its markdown body.

example.bodyMarkdown: # Rules\n\nOne QSO per park per day…

get.description: The published policy version. Policy is immutable once published — activity and geodata read it to decide whether a submission is valid, so a silent edit would change the rules of an award already in progress.

post.description: Creates a `draft`. Nothing is visible to participants until it is published, which is a separate, reviewable act.

patch.description: Only a `draft` is editable. An active programme's name and categories are frozen, because changing them would reinterpret awards already issued.

put.summary: Replace the categories a programme accepts
put.description: `PUT` because it replaces the whole set: a category removed here stops being valid for new entities in this programme. Existing entities keep theirs, which is why this is a set replacement rather than per-item add/remove — the UI shows a checklist, not a list of deltas.

200.description: The programme with its new category set.

post.description: Makes the programme visible and usable, and publishes `core.programme.published.v1`. `activity` and `geodata` consume that event to know which programme a submission may reference.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Publishing an active programme is a no-op that republishes no event.

post.description: Stops new activity without deleting anything. Existing activations and awards keep working; the programme disappears from the public list and publishes `core.programme.archived.v1`.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Archiving an archived programme is a no-op.

post.description: Created as a draft. Publication is a separate operation, so a half-written rules page never becomes the public rules page.

example.bodyMarkdown: # Rules\n\nOne QSO per summit per day…
# Rules\n\nOne QSO per summit per day…

post.x-idempotency-reason: Publishing a published page is a no-op.

example.bodyMarkdown: # Rules\n\nOne QSO per summit per day…

200.description: One page of drafts, newest first.

post.description: The version number is assigned from the current published version, so two drafts cannot claim the same successor.

post.summary: Submit a policy draft for review
post.description: A draft cannot be published by its own author; it moves to `in_review` and needs a different administrator to approve it.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Submitting a submitted draft is refused, not repeated.
Approving an approved draft is a no-op.
Rejecting a rejected draft is a no-op.

example.reason: Duplicate window conflicts with the published rule for 2026.

post.description: Copies the draft's rules into an immutable `programme_policy_version`. From here the rules can only be superseded by a new version, never edited — an award relies on the rules it was evaluated against.
post.x-idempotency-reason: A published draft is immutable; a repeat is refused.

get.description: Scope `identity.admins.manage`. The list shows MFA state, because an administrator without a confirmed factor cannot sign in and the console must say who that is rather than leaving it to be discovered.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text over display name and address.

200.description: The account with its grants and session summary.

get.description:
The union of the scopes from every open grant, plus the grants themselves.
This is the answer an interface needs to decide what to show, and the
answer `core` itself uses when it evaluates a request — the same function,
so the console cannot offer a button the service would refuse.

Scope `identity.admins.manage`. Reading somebody else's authority is part of
managing it, and a scope that only lets you read what you can already see is
not a control.

post.summary: Grant a role to an administrator
post.description:
Two rules make this safe, and both are checked at write time rather than
relied on from the UI:

1. **The grant must be a subset of the actor's own scopes.** A holder of
   `identity.admins.manage` who can grant `identity.admins.manage` to
   anyone else has root, whatever the scope is called.
2. **Re-authentication within five minutes** is required, so a stolen
   session cannot be used to mint an accomplice.

Publishing `core.role.changed.v1` invalidates cached scopes for the
affected sessions.

403.description:
One of two refusals, both of which are the rule rather than a failure:

- `about:blank#scope-not-held` — the role carries a scope the actor does
  not hold. `detail` lists them. This is what stops
  `identity.admins.manage` from being equivalent to root.
- `about:blank#forbidden` — the actor lacks `identity.admins.manage`
  entirely, so the route class refused before the body was read.

scopeNotHeld.summary: The actor cannot grant what they do not hold

value.title: Scope not held
value.detail: The role programme_admin carries identity.admins.manage, which this account does not hold.

forbidden.summary: The actor cannot manage administrators at all

value.title: Forbidden
value.detail: This account holds no role with an administrator scope.

delete.description: Refused if it would remove the actor's own last administrator role, so the console cannot be locked out by one click.

409.description: The revocation would leave the actor with no administrator role at all, so the console could be locked out with one click. `409` rather than `403` because the request is well formed and the actor *is* allowed to revoke grants; this particular removal is what the state forbids.

example.title: Conflict
example.detail: This is your last administrator role. Grant another before revoking this one.

post.description: Clears the confirmed factor and issues a recovery code, so an administrator who lost their device can enrol again. Requires re-authentication within five minutes, records actor and target, and revokes the target's sessions.

202.description: The factor is cleared and the target's sessions are revoked.

post.description: Suspension blocks sign-in and revokes open sessions immediately. It does not delete the account or its audit trail.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Suspension is a state, not a count; a repeat leaves the same state.
Reactivation is a state, not a count.

get.description: Every field change with actor, before and after. This is what makes an escalation detectable after the fact rather than only preventable in advance.

200.description: One page of security events, newest first.

delete.summary: Revoke one of an administrator's sessions
delete.description: Per-session, not "sign out everywhere": a suspicious session is identified by its user agent and address and revoked on its own.

get.description: Scope `identity.participants.manage`. Thousands of rows, so the list is searchable and filterable from the start, and each row shows whether the address is verified and whether mail has bounced — that is what turns "I never got the email" into a five-second answer.

200.description: The account with its callsigns and delivery state.

post.description: Callsign verification is the main support job. The decision is attributed: evidence, reviewer and time. Repeating it returns the same decision rather than creating a second one.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The decision is recorded once; a repeat returns it unchanged.
The decision is recorded once; a repeat returns it unchanged.

example.reason: The uploaded document is unreadable; please re-submit a scan.

post.description: Reversible, and it does not delete anything: activations and QSOs survive with their references detached. A hard delete is a retention job, never a support button. Publishes `core.account.closed.v1`, which is how `activity` and `geodata` learn to detach their copies.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Closing a closed account is a no-op that republishes no event.
Reactivation is a state, not a count.

post.summary: Resend the verification email for a participant
post.description: The support action for "I never got the email". Supersedes any outstanding token, and reports `202` even when the address is suppressed — the administrator sees the suppression state on the account instead of guessing why nothing arrived.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Rate-limited per account; a second request supersedes the first token.

get.description: One ledger for every email and in-app message, in every state. This replaces six tables across two databases that each retried on their own.

200.description: One page of notifications, newest first.

get.summary: Read one notification with its delivery attempts

200.description: The notification and every attempt made.

post.summary: Queue a failed notification for another attempt
post.description: Creates a fresh job against the same notification. Idempotency matters here more than anywhere: a double-click that sends a second copy of a delivery email is a support ticket, so a key is required.

get.description: Addresses that must not receive mail: hard-bounced, complained, or suppressed by hand. Keyed by address rather than by notification, so the list survives the account being closed.

post.description: Idempotent on the address, which is the primary key — adding a suppressed address twice leaves one row.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The address is the primary key; a repeat updates nothing.

delete.description: Marks the suppression released rather than deleting the row, so the history of why an account missed mail is not lost.

get.description:
Anonymous for published entities; an administrator may filter by every
status. Filters combine, and the result is cursor-paginated in catalogue
order so a map viewport request is cheap.

`bbox` is `minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat` in WGS 84 — the same order as a
GeoJSON bounding box, so a client does not have to remember a second
convention.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category code, as declared by the programme in `core`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only `published` is visible without an administrator session; any other value is refused rather than silently downgraded.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text over name and slug.

post.description: For a place an administrator adds by hand, not for bulk loads — bulk work goes through the import pipeline so it arrives with candidates, evidence and a review. Created as `draft`; publication is a separate act.

get.description: Includes the full geometry. List responses carry only the centroid, so a map request for 200 parks is not 200 polygons, and a detail request is where the shape is actually needed.

patch.description:
Carries the `revision` the client read. The server compares it, applies
the change and returns the new revision; a mismatch is
`409 about:blank#revision-conflict` with both numbers in the detail, so a
reviewer knows to re-read rather than to retry blindly.

Editing does not use a staging table. A staging table was one of three
overlapping mechanisms in the legacy system, and a single entity with a
revision needs none of them.

200.description: The updated entity, with its new revision.

get.description: Every change with actor, action, before and after. Actor ids are `core` account ids held as opaque values — no foreign key, because the account may be closed while the history must survive it.

200.description: One page of audit events, newest first.

get.summary: Read where an entity's data came from
get.description: One row per source that contributed: the snapshot (the exact bytes an import read), the source's own feature id, and a confidence. This is what makes an attribution claim answerable a year later.

post.description: Makes the entity visible to participants and publishes `geodata.entity.published.v1`, which is how `activity` learns that the place can be activated.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Publishing a published entity is a no-op that republishes no event.

post.description: Hides the entity from the public catalogue and publishes `geodata.entity.retired.v1`. Activations that used it keep it: `activity` captured the name and elevation at activation start, so retiring a place does not rewrite anyone's log.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Retiring a retired entity is a no-op that republishes no event.

example.reason: Merged into the adjacent entity after a boundary correction.

post.summary: Attach an image to an entity
post.description: Returns a presigned `PUT` URL. The client uploads the bytes to object storage, then calls this endpoint again with the completed attachment to confirm. The second step exists because a presigned URL proves intent, not that the object arrived.

201.description: The attachment record and where to put the bytes.

413.description: The declared size exceeds the attachment ceiling.

example.title: Attachment too large
example.detail: 12 MiB declared; the attachment ceiling is 8 MiB.

get.description: A participant sees only their own proposals. The administrator view of the same rows is `/v1/admin/proposals`; one resource, two audiences, one table.

200.description: One page of proposals, newest first.

post.summary: Propose a new place or a correction
post.description: Participants cannot write the catalogue. A proposal is a request for review that carries the evidence, and an administrator decides it. This is the only write path a participant has into `geodata`.

example.note: The northern boundary ends at the river, not the track.

get.summary: Read one of the participant's proposals

200.description: The proposal with its decision, if there is one.

example.note: The northern boundary ends at the river, not the track.

post.description: Only while it is `open`. A decided proposal is history.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Withdrawing a withdrawn proposal is a no-op.

get.description: Scope `geodata.review`. The legacy system's conflation endpoints required only a valid token; this one requires the scope, and the scope is checked in `core` and cached per session.

200.description: One page of proposals, oldest first so nothing is forgotten.

post.summary: Approve a proposal and apply it
post.description: Applies the proposed change to the entity in one transaction with the decision, so an approved proposal and its effect cannot disagree.
post.x-idempotency-reason: A decided proposal cannot be decided again; a repeat returns the decision.
A decided proposal cannot be decided again.

example.note: The submitted boundary matches the current published shape.

example.decisionNote: The submitted boundary matches the current published shape.

post.description:
A 1 GiB shapefile over a poor connection is a real case, so uploads are
multipart and resumable. The session records the declared size and
checksum up front: a client that cannot state them is not uploading a
file it knows anything about, and a mismatch at completion is caught
before an import ever reads the bytes.

201.description: The session, with the first part's upload URL.

413.description: The declared size exceeds the import ceiling.

example.title: Upload exceeds the ceiling
example.detail: 2 GiB declared; the ceiling is 1 GiB.

post.summary: Sign one part of an upload
post.description: Returns a presigned URL for a single part. Called per part, so a connection that drops at part 7 resumes at part 7.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Signing a URL twice issues a second valid URL; nothing is created.

201.description: A presigned URL for the part.

post.description: Assembles the parts, verifies the checksum against the one declared at the start, and returns the snapshot to use in `POST /v1/imports`. A checksum mismatch is `409`: the bytes that arrived are not the bytes the client meant to send, and an import must not be the thing that discovers that.
post.x-idempotency-reason: A completed session cannot be completed again; a repeat returns the same snapshot.

200.description: The completed session and the snapshot it produced.
One page of runs, newest first.

post.summary: Start an import run from a snapshot
post.description: Creates the run and queues `import.preprocess` as a job in `ops.job`. The job is the queue: there is no separate broker, and a worker claims it with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` exactly as a broker's durable consumer would.
Stops the pipeline and discards the run's candidates. A run already in `review` is cancelled the same way; nothing was published, so nothing needs undoing.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Cancelling a cancelled run is a no-op.

get.description: The review screen. Each candidate is one feature from the source, in the state the validator left it, with the reason when it is invalid. Filtering by state is what makes a 4 000-feature run reviewable.
Errors are per candidate and carry a code, so a systematic problem — every feature missing a name, say — is visible as a pattern rather than as 4 000 rows to read.

items.message: Ring 1 self-intersects at (-8.31, 41.72); repaired with a zero-width buffer.

get.description: Each row is a proposed match between an imported feature and an existing entity, with a score and the reasons for it. `unresolved` rows are the ones a reviewer must decide before the run can publish.

post.description: Records `merge`, `new` or `skip` for one candidate. Scope `geodata.review` is required per request, not merely a valid token — the legacy system got this wrong on exactly this endpoint.
post.x-idempotency-reason: The decision is stored once per candidate; a repeat overwrites the same row.

post.summary: Promote a reviewed run into the catalogue
post.description:
Promotes the run's resolved candidates in batches of at most 300, so one
transaction stays short enough to reason about. Every promoted entity
writes its `entity_provenance` row in the same transaction as the entity,
which is what makes attribution answerable later.

Refused while any candidate is still `unresolved`: publishing a run with
an undecided merge would double the catalogue.

202.description: Promotion queued; the run moves to `publishing`.

post.description: The licence and attribution are required fields, not notes: an entity derived from this source inherits them, and a catalogue that cannot state where it came from cannot be published.

get.description: One row per fetch: the exact bytes an import read, with a feature count and a checksum. Provenance points here, so "which version of the source produced this geometry" has an answer.

200.description: One page of snapshots, newest first.

get.description: A schedule is a row with a cron expression and a unique `(kind, scheduled_for)` slot, not a cron loop inside a container. Two replicas therefore cannot both fetch the same source at 03:00.

patch.summary: Enable, disable or retime a schedule

get.description:
Anonymous. Mapbox Vector Tile, generated from the published catalogue
with a `ST_AsMVT` query, so the map does not paginate a million polygons
through a JSON endpoint.

Tiles are cacheable and carry a long `Cache-Control`: the geometry for a
published entity changes rarely, and a tile is regenerated only when the
catalogue does.

parameters.name: programme
parameters.description: Restrict the tile to one programme.

Cache-Control.description: Cacheable for a day; a catalogue change invalidates by the ETag rather than by a purge.

get.description: Own activations only. An administrator reading someone else's log goes through the account-scoped route rather than through a widened version of this one, so a participant request cannot be turned into an administrator-shaped query by a parameter.

200.description: One page of activations, newest first.

post.description:
Captures the place's name and elevation as they are now, so a later
rename in `geodata` cannot rewrite this activation's history.

Only one activation may be `active` per callsign at a time — two open
activations from one operator is a double-counting bug, not a feature.
The entity must be `published`; a retired place cannot start an
activation. That check asks `geodata` once and caches for the request.
Ends the activation, freezes its counts and publishes `activity.activation.closed.v1`. An award evaluation is queued as a job, not run inline: the response should not wait on a rule engine.
post.x-idempotency-reason: An activation can only be closed once; a repeat is refused with 409.

post.description: For an activation that should not count — started by mistake, or at the wrong place. Distinct from closing: a cancelled activation is excluded from statistics and from award evaluation, and the distinction is kept because "I made a mistake" and "I finished" are different facts.
post.x-idempotency-reason: Cancelling a cancelled activation is a no-op.

example.reason: Started at the wrong park; re-logging from the correct one.

200.description: One page of contacts, in logged order.

post.description: Appends one contact to an active activation. Logging against a closed or cancelled activation is refused: the counts are frozen at close, and a late write would make the total disagree with itself.

patch.description: A direct correction while the activation is open — the operator is still there and knows what they typed. Once the activation is closed, changes go through `/v1/qsos/{qsoId}/corrections`, which records a request and a decision.

delete.summary: Delete a contact logged in error
delete.description: Only while the activation is open. Deleting is for a typo — a contact that never happened. A contact that happened but was logged wrongly is a correction.

post.summary: Request a correction to a closed contact
post.description: Records what should change and why. The original value stays until an administrator decides, so the record shows both what was claimed and what was changed.

example.reason: The 20 m contact was actually on 40 m; logged too quickly.

get.description: Scope `activity.review`. Oldest first: a correction queue that nobody reads is a queue that never drains.

post.summary: Approve a correction and apply it
post.description: Applies the change in the same transaction as the decision, then re-evaluates the affected award progress as a queued job.
post.x-idempotency-reason: A decided correction cannot be decided again.

example.note: The logger's ADIF file confirms 40 m.

example.decisionNote: The logger's ADIF file confirms 40 m.

post.x-idempotency-reason: A decided correction cannot be decided again.

example.note: The uploaded log shows 20 m for this contact.

example.decisionNote: The uploaded log shows 20 m for this contact.

200.description: One page of imports, newest first.

post.summary: Import an ADIF or CSV log
post.description:
The file is uploaded to object storage first — bytes never pass through
this API — and this call supplies the object key. Rows are parsed into
QSOs, and each row's outcome is recorded so a rejected line is visible
with its line number and reason instead of disappearing.

A partially accepted import is a normal outcome: 198 of 200 lines
accepted is a successful import with two problems to fix.

413.description: The declared size exceeds the log-import ceiling.

example.title: Log file too large
example.detail: 64 MiB declared; the log ceiling is 32 MiB.

get.summary: List the per-row outcome of an import
get.description: One row per line in the file, with the outcome and, when rejected, the reason. This is what makes "198 accepted, 2 rejected" actionable.

items.message: Worked callsign 'EA1ABC??' is not a valid callsign.

get.description: Anonymous. A participant needs to know what they can claim, and the rules are public.
Includes the condition tree, so a participant can see why they do or do not qualify rather than being told only the outcome.

get.summary: Read the signed-in account's progress toward an award
get.description: A materialised evaluation, with the time it was built. Re-evaluated when an activation closes or a correction is approved, never on read — a rule engine running inside a GET is how a page load becomes a transaction.

post.description: Only for an award whose progress is satisfied. Requesting an award that is not yet earned is refused rather than queued — a queue of impossible requests is a support burden nobody asked for.

get.summary: List the awards the account holds
get.description: Under `/v1/awards/` rather than `/v1/me/` so that every route prefix has exactly one owning service. `/v1/me/**` belongs to `core`; a participant's awards are `activity`'s rows, and folding them under `/v1/me` would make the gateway's prefix table ambiguous at the one place it must not be.

200.description: One page of issuances, newest first.

get.description: Returns a short-lived presigned URL for the certificate rather than the bytes, so the endpoint stays cacheable and the certificate is fetched once.

post.description: The rules are a condition tree stored as JSONB and evaluated by the worker. Creating a definition does not evaluate anyone's progress; the `award.evaluate` job does, queued when the definition becomes active.

patch.description: A published definition is versioned: changing the rules of an award that has already been issued would reinterpret a certificate someone holds. An edit to an active award creates version `n+1`; the old version stays for the issuances that used it.

get.description: Scope `awards.manage`. Oldest first, because the queue is the work.

post.x-idempotency-reason: A decided request cannot be decided again.
A decided request cannot be decided again.

example.note: Three of the claimed entities were retired before the activations.

post.description: Generates the certificate into object storage and records the issuance. Publishes `activity.award.issued.v1`, which is how `core` learns to send the notification — `activity` does not send mail.

get.description: The latest materialised snapshot for this account, with `builtAt` so a stale number is visibly stale rather than quietly wrong.

`scope` narrows what `scopeId` means: an account, a programme, or an entity. One endpoint with three meanings rather than three endpoints with three shapes — the payload is a bag either way, and the client picks the fields it knows.
Reads the materialised `leaderboard_entry` rows for the newest snapshot. A leaderboard over 10⁷ QSOs computed per request is not a leaderboard, it is an outage.

200.description: One page of ranked entries, best first.

participantBearer.description: Participant access token, `aud=participant`, 15 minute lifetime. Obtain it from `POST /v1/auth/login`. The gateway rejects it on `/v1/admin/**`.

adminBearer.description: Administrator access token, `aud=admin`, 10 minute lifetime. Obtain it from `POST /v1/admin/auth/login`, which requires a confirmed second factor. The gateway rejects it outside `/v1/admin/**`.

participantSession.name: __Host-myota_sid
participantSession.description: Participant refresh session cookie. `__Host-` forces Secure, forbids Domain, and pins the path to `/`, so the two audiences cannot overwrite each other in one browser.

adminSession.name: __Host-myota_admin_sid
adminSession.description: Administrator refresh session cookie. Separate name, separate lifetime (30 min idle, 8 h absolute), separate audience.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque position returned as `nextCursor` by the previous page. Do not parse or construct one: the encoding is a service implementation detail and may change without a version bump. `null` in a response means the collection is exhausted.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Values above the maximum are clamped rather than rejected — an oversized page is a caller mistake, not a reason to fail a read. The maximum matches `lsMaxPageItems` in `libs/limits`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Caller-chosen key, unique per logical operation. A replay with the same key and the same body returns the stored response and creates nothing; the same key with a different body is `422 idempotency-key-reused`. Records expire after 24 hours.

RequestId.description: Echo of `X-Request-ID`. The gateway generates one if the caller did not supply it, and every `Problem` response repeats it so a report can be traced to a log line.

ProblemBadRequest.description: The request is malformed or fails field validation.

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: One or more fields are invalid.

errors.message: A callsign is 3 to 10 characters, A-Z 0-9 and /.

ProblemUnauthorized.description: No credential, an expired one, or a token whose `aud` does not match the route class. Never a redirect: a redirect would disclose which audience the route expects.

example.title: Wrong audience for this route
example.detail: This session is a participant session; the route requires an administrator session.

ProblemForbidden.description: Authenticated, correct audience, insufficient scope — or an administrator operation that needs re-authentication within the last five minutes.

example.title: Missing scope
example.detail: geodata.review is required, and this account does not hold it for programme:7d2c…

ProblemNotFound.description: No such resource, or one the caller is not allowed to see.

ProblemConflict.description: The resource is not in a state that permits the change, or the caller's `revision` is stale.

value.title: Activation is already closed
value.detail: An activation can only be closed once.

value.title: Entity was modified by someone else
value.detail: Sent revision 7, current revision 9. Re-read and reapply.

ProblemUnprocessable.description: The request is well formed but cannot be applied — most often an `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body.

example.title: Idempotency-Key reused with a different body
example.detail: The key 4f2a… was first used with a different payload. Use a fresh key for a different operation.

ProblemTooManyRequests.description: Rate limited. Traefik enforces the edge limit; `core` enforces the per-account login limit, which must be global and authoritative and so lives in the database rather than in a replica's memory.

example.title: Too many requests
example.detail: 5 failed administrator logins in 15 minutes. Try again later.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem detail. Every error response in this API is `application/problem+json` with this shape — there is no second error envelope, and no endpoint returns a bare string on failure.

type.description: A URI identifying the problem class. This API uses fragment identifiers relative to `about:blank`, so `type` is comparable without a network fetch.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem class. Stable per `type`; do not show two titles for one type.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated so a log line is complete.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation for this occurrence. May name the field, the conflicting revision, or the scope that was missing.

instance.description: The specific occurrence, when it is addressable.

requestId.description: Matches `X-Request-ID`, so a user report can be traced to one request in the logs.

errors.description: Field-level failures. Present when `type` is `about:blank#validation-failed`; absent otherwise.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer into the request body — `/callsign`, or `/programmeIds/2`. A pointer, not a dotted path, so a client can apply it without re-parsing the document.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code, stable across releases.

CursorPage.description: The shape every collection returns. No endpoint returns a bare array: a bare array cannot grow a `total`, an `etag`, or a second cursor without breaking every client. Concrete pages extend this with `allOf` and narrow `items` to their element type.

items.description: The page's elements, newest or most relevant first according to the endpoint. Ordering is documented per operation.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` means there is no next page — it is not an empty-string sentinel.

Rejection.description: A free-text reason attached to a decision. Required wherever a refusal is recorded, because "no" without a reason is not something a participant can act on.

Decision.description: An administrator's note on a decision. Optional on approval, where the decision speaks for itself.

Accepted.description: Acknowledgement for operations that have nothing else to say.

AccountScopes.description: An account's effective authority: the union of the scopes from every open grant, and the grants those came from. The two are returned together because an interface needs both — the scopes to decide what to show, the grants to decide what can be revoked.

scopes.description: Deduplicated union across open grants, sorted.

password.description: At least 12 characters, checked against a breached-password list. Length over composition rules: a passphrase of four words is both stronger and easier to type than a 10-character puzzle.

participationType.description: An operator transmits; an SWL only listens. The distinction changes which programme rules apply, not which account exists.

accountId.description: Returned even when the address was already registered. The real account id is not disclosed, but the shape is identical so the response cannot be used as an enumeration oracle.

token.description: The raw token from the email. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so a database read cannot be turned into an account takeover.

password.description: The current password. A session alone must not be able to move an account to another mailbox.

accessToken.description: JWT with `aud=participant`, 15 minute lifetime. Also set as an `HttpOnly` cookie by the gateway; returned in the body so a non-browser client can use it.

refreshExpiresAt.description: The refresh token's absolute expiry; idle expiry is enforced server-side.

scopes.description: Effective scopes at issue time. Not authoritative for later requests — `core` re-evaluates, and a role change invalidates the cache through `core.role.changed.v1`.

MfaChallenge.description: A sign-in that needs a second factor before it becomes a session.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes. The challenge is bound to the password verification that created it.

AdminLoginResult.description: Either a challenge or a session. Discriminated on `status` so a client cannot mistake one for the other, and so "needs a second factor" is not modelled as an error.

code.description: A 6-digit TOTP code, a WebAuthn assertion, or a recovery code. One field because it is one decision.

MfaEnrolment.description: A pending enrolment. Nothing is confirmed until a code proves the factor works — an interrupted enrolment must not lock anyone out.

secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret. Absent for WebAuthn.

code.description: A second factor, when the account has more than one method.

audience.description: Which login produced this session. The admin UI uses it to decide whether to offer the console; it never substitutes for a server-side check.

evidenceObjectKey.description: Key of a file already uploaded to object storage. Bytes never pass through this API: uploads are presigned, so a 20 MiB scan does not become an API request that has to be buffered.

current.description: True for the session making the request.

geometryPolicy.description: Which geometry types this category accepts, so an import cannot put a polygon where a summit point belongs.

PolicyVersion.description: An immutable published policy. Editing it in place would change the rules an already-evaluated award was granted under.

roleCode.description: The scopes this grants must be a subset of the actor's own. That is checked at write time, not left to the interface.

mfa.description: Visible because an administrator without a confirmed factor cannot sign in. The console must show who is blocked.

emailBounced.description: True when the address is on the suppression list. Answers "why did nothing arrive" without a mail-log search.

template.description: An allowlisted template id, never caller-supplied body text — otherwise the notification system is an open relay.

attempts.description: Bounded at 8, then the notification is `dead`.

providerId.description: The SMTP message id, used to correlate bounces.

GeoJsonGeometry.description: A GeoJSON geometry object. Validated against the programme's `geometryPolicy` for the category before it is stored, so an import cannot put a polygon where a summit point belongs.

coordinates.description: GeoJSON coordinates. Depth depends on `type`, which is why this is not narrowed further here.

EntitySummary.description: An entity in a list. Deliberately without geometry: a map viewport of 200 entities should not be 200 polygons. `centroid` is enough to place a marker, and the detail endpoint is where the shape lives.

programmeId.description: Opaque reference to `core.programme`; no foreign key crosses the database boundary.

revision.description: Optimistic concurrency token. Every edit carries it.

EntityUpdate.description: A partial edit. `revision` is required and is not optional-by-omission: an edit without a revision is an edit without a concurrency check, which is the behaviour this design removed.

sizeBytes.description: 8 MiB. Attachments are images and small documents, not datasets — those go through the import pipeline.

submittedBy.description: The `core` account id. Present only in the administrator view.

status.description: `review` is a status, not a stage. "Awaiting an administrator" is not something the pipeline does, and modelling it as a stage made the legacy state machine 11 states wide.

entityId.description: Opaque reference to `geo.entity`; no foreign key crosses the boundary.

entityName.description: Captured when the activation started. A later rename in `geodata` does not rewrite this — a log records what was true when it was written.

callsign.description: A verified callsign belonging to the caller. An unverified one is refused: the whole point of verification is that an activation is attributable.

startedAt.description: Defaults to now. May not be in the future.

endedAt.description: Defaults to now. May not be before the start.

QsoUpdate.description: A partial correction while the activation is open.

changes.description: Field name to new value. Validated against `QsoUpdate`.

sizeBytes.description: 32 MiB. A log is text; anything larger is a dataset.

rules.description: A condition tree, evaluated by the `award.evaluate` job. Left as a free-form object here because each node type carries different fields; the shape is documented in `docs/architecture/`.

accountId.description: Present in the administrator view only.

certificateUrl.description: A short-lived presigned URL. The certificate lives in object storage, not in this API and not in the database.

builtAt.description: When the snapshot was materialised. Shown to the user, so a stale number is visibly stale rather than quietly wrong.

displayName.description: Captured in the snapshot, so a rename does not reshuffle a historical leaderboard.

externalDocs.description: Architecture, decisions and the contract rules.
